chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Fuzayl ibn Uthman, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The believer is between two fears: a sin that has passed, not knowing what Allah has done with it, and a lifespan that remains, not knowing what he will acquire from destruction during it. Thus, he does not wake up except as fearful, and nothing corrects him except fear.
ai.seo_question: What are the two fears that define the spiritual state of a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to illustrate the dialectic of 'khawf' (fear) as a stabilizing force for the believer, who oscillates between uncertainty about the acceptance of past deeds and the potential pitfalls of future actions. This state of vigilant anxiety is not paralyzing but rather constructive, serving as the essential spiritual mechanism that prevents complacency and ensures the rectification of one's character and deeds.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Fuzayl Bin usman, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘A ‘Momin’ (Believer) is between the two fears – sins of the past, without knowing what Allahazwj would be Doing with regards to it, and the life which has remained, not knowing what he would be attaining during it, from the destruction. Thus, he will not wake up in the morning except as fearful, and nothing would correct his (affairs - best) except for the fear’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Fudayl ibn ‘Uthman from abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“A believer lives in two frightening conditions. In his life he is concerned about his sins of the past about which he does not know how Allah has decided. He is also worried about his future, for not knowing what kind of destructive sins he may get involved in. Therefore, he is always fearful and nothing serves his best interest except fear.”
